title: RescueSpeech: A German Corpus for Speech Recognition in Search and Rescue Domain
why_promising: Primary non-singing German speech recorded from native speakers during simulated search-and-rescue exercises. Zenodo describes the recordings as manually annotated. The v2 deposit is open under CC BY-NC 4.0 and exposes a README plus ASR and speech-enhancement archives. The ASR release contains 2412 original clean utterances alongside synthesized noisy counterparts; the enhancement release is explicitly augmentation-derived from clean utterances. The primary clean recordings may qualify if the supplied annotations are manual phonetic/production annotations rather than transcription-only labels.
open_question: Keep in HIGH review until archive-level inspection isolates the original clean recordings and establishes exactly what 'manually annotated' means. Do not admit synthesized noisy utterances, external AudioSet noise, or augmentation-derived enhancement material as primary production. Inspect README/archive members for annotation formats, timing/boundary provenance, speaker/utterance metadata, and any manually verified segmental/prosodic/acoustic measurements; deduplicate all noisy derivatives against their clean parent utterances.
